The widgets on this site are hand-written JavaScript on top of dp-core. This page draws the same
kind of picture in R with htmlwidgets, to see what that route costs and when it is the better
choice. The data are the conditional pmf of K_100 and the size-biased weight density
f_SB(w | alpha) = alpha (1 − w)^(alpha − 1) for 40 values of alpha between 0.1 and 20, computed
with DPprior 2.0.0; E[K_100 | alpha = 1] = 5.1874 agrees with the site's golden value to every
printed digit.

## plotly: one frame per alpha

```{=html}
<iframe src="../../apps/htmlwidgets/plotly-alpha-sweep.html" title="plotly: the pmf of K_100 given alpha and the size-biased weight density, one animation frame per alpha"
        loading="lazy" style="width:100%;height:560px;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:8px;background:white"></iframe>
```

Press Play or drag the slider. As alpha grows, the pmf of K_100 moves to the right and the
weight density moves toward 0: the count and the weight are two lenses on the same alpha
([C-04](../bridge/two-lenses.qmd) does this live, for any J).

## ggiraph: hover for the numbers

![E[K_100 | alpha] against alpha on a log scale: 1.5 at alpha = 0.1, 5.19 at alpha = 1 and 36 at alpha = 20. In the interactive version each point's tooltip adds Pr(W_SB > .5 | alpha) = .5^alpha.](../../apps/htmlwidgets/ggiraph-alpha-sweep.png){width=100%}

The interactive ggiraph version adds a tooltip to each point with E[K_100 | alpha] and
Pr(W_SB > .5 | alpha) = .5^alpha. It is built and measured by the same R script, but ggiraph's
JavaScript is licensed GPL-3 and this site's code is MIT, so the site shows the chart as a
picture.

## What each route costs (measured)

::: {.dpx-table-scroll tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="What each route costs, scrollable table"}
| Route | What ships | Size | From `file://` | Interaction | Use it when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dp-core widget (this site) | one script bundle per widget + vendored D3 and Plot | bundles 10 KB to 635 KB (median 22 KB); D3 280 KB + Plot 209 KB, shared | yes | anything, computed live in the browser | the viewer should steer the model |
| plotly, shared `lib/` (this page) | page with all 40 frames (564 KB) + `lib/` (4.4 MB, of which plotly.js 3.5 MB) | 4.9 MB | yes (plain scripts) | frames, zoom, hover | a quick animated look at precomputed frames |
| plotly, self-contained | one HTML file | 4.35 MB | yes | same | sending one file |
| ggiraph, self-contained (not shipped here: GPL-3) | one HTML file with an SVG | 0.30 MB (with fonts left out) | yes | hover, select | a ggplot2 figure with tooltips, where GPL-3 is acceptable |
| htmlwidgets inside a Quarto page (knitr) | the same widgets, rendered into the page | as above | yes | same | a document that runs R anyway; not used here, so the site render needs no R |
:::

Three lessons from building it. ggiraph's default font set embeds the Liberation fonts
(3 × 6.2 MB = 18.6 MB) and a system font set would copy system font files, so the widget is
saved without font files and the browser uses its own sans-serif. Licences travel with the
libraries: ggiraph's JavaScript is GPL-3 and htmltools' `fill.css` is GPL (>= 2), so neither
is published here (the plotly page lays out without `fill.css`). And plotly's subplot with
animation frames warns that "scatter objects don't have frameOrder"; the warning is harmless and
the frames play. In a reveal.js deck both widgets go in as an iframe, like the deck's local
iframe slide.

## How it is made (R, not run on this site)

```r
# r-export/08_plotly_frames.R (excerpt)
ALPHA <- sort(unique(c(exp(seq(log(0.1), log(20), length.out = 38)), 1, 10)))   # 40 frames
pmf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ALPHA, function(a)
  data.frame(alpha = a, k = 1:60, p = pmf_K_given_alpha(100, a, logS)[-1][1:60])))
bars <- plot_ly(pmf, x = ~k, y = ~p, frame = ~signif(alpha, 3), type = "bar")
line <- plot_ly(fsb, x = ~w, y = ~f, frame = ~signif(alpha, 3), type = "scatter", mode = "lines")
subplot(bars, line, widths = c(0.6, 0.4)) |>
  animation_opts(frame = 500, transition = 250, redraw = FALSE)
girafe(ggobj = gg, font_set = gdtools::font_set(sans = "Helvetica"))   # measured, not shipped (GPL-3)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(w, "plotly-alpha-sweep.html", selfcontained = FALSE, libdir = "lib")
```

The data behind both widgets are in `data/precomputed/alpha_sweep_J100.json`.
